## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
No trials have run yet. The starting architecture scores 0 on dev with both seeds. With the default recipe the budget gives only 32 PPO updates (4096 samples each), which is probably too few to learn ordered, exact placements and when to call DONE. From the code: the observation is [B, 4Z+3, Y, X], each action index is type×(Y·X)+y·X+x, and DONE is last. The starting network uses about 50k multiply-accumulates per cell, so a fully convolutional 3x3 network 32 channels wide (about 46k) costs no samples (r≤1). This round splits the effects: the recipe alone on the starting architecture (more updates, higher gamma and lambda, lower entropy); a new normalised residual network with a spatial per-type head on the same recipe; and the new network with 1 PPO epoch for about 3.25x the samples. If dev stays near 0, rank by training success and by how many seeds succeed.

### Round 2
All four runs scored 0 on both dev and training success: the starting architecture, the update-rich recipe, and the residual-conv spatial head trained with 1 or 2 PPO epochs. Even 426k samples with about 104 updates gave no exact builds during training, so the number of samples and updates alone is probably not the bottleneck. One possible cause, which I have not verified, is a mismatch the note warns about. Both spatial heads assume a top-left anchor and a type-major action order. If the anchor or the action ordering differs, every logit lands on the wrong cell and greedy exact builds become nearly impossible. This round tests ways to make the head robust to that. A symmetric 3x3 head works for any anchor within one cell. The mask, reshaped into one channel per brick type, is fed as input; it is aligned with the action indices, so it shows which positions and edges are legal. A flat low-rank head can learn any action ordering. A third candidate tests the default number of epochs with more entropy.

### Round 3
All six trials score 0 on dev and 0 on training success on both seeds. The spatial heads, the mask input, the flat head, 1 vs 2 vs 4 epochs and the lr changes all show no difference, so the results cannot rank any of them. Two explanations fit. (1) Collapse onto DONE: random placements earn negative reward on average while DONE earns 0. DONE's advantage is then positive in almost every state, so the policy may learn to end episodes early before it learns good placements. Our low ent_coef of 0.005 makes this more likely. (2) Representation: the trunks must learn a conjunction across layers ("missing at layer z AND landing height equals z under the whole footprint") from mixed channels, which is hard with few samples. This round tests a higher entropy coefficient on the r2c1 net (recipe only). It also tests a new per-layer 2D-conv architecture that makes that conjunction local, run once with the old recipe and once with higher entropy.

### Round 4
All 9 trials scored 0 on both dev and training success, on both seeds. Changing the recipe (1, 2 or 4 epochs; entropy 0.005 to 0.03; gamma 0.95 to 0.99), the head (2x2, 3x3, hybrid flat, per-layer) and the trunk made no visible difference, so nothing can be ranked. A random policy rarely gives up early, and correct placements earn positive reward, so collapsing onto DONE is an unlikely cause (r3c1's higher entropy also did not help). The more likely blockers are per-step accuracy within this budget, or a hidden mismatch between action indices and cells. My residual trunks dropped the starting architecture's footprint pooling head (max, min and mean over each brick's footprint), which fits landing height and the all-cells-missing test. This last round therefore combines that pooling head with the normalised residual trunk and mask input. One variant adds a layout-free per-type linear head, and one tests the 1-epoch, maximum-sample recipe on the same network.
